notes: Printed Spellcaster (Beasts or Heavens) requires an explicit Lore choice; core Spellcaster supplies matching Channelling and Language (Magick). Life is a rare GM choice described in the text, not an extra caste grant.

traits.name: Afraid
traits.text: The creature gains Fear of the Target. When encountered, they must make an Extended Psychology Test (page 183). Until their SL equals or exceeds the Target’s Fear Rating, the creature cannot gain Momentum, and Melee Attacks made against them by the Target benefit from Advantage. See page 183 for Fear rules.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.text: The creature is as at home in water as they are on land. They have the Swim Skill, add +1 SL to all Swim Tests, and move at full Movement through water.

traits.name: Animosity
traits.text: The creature dislikes the Target. When the creature encounters the object of its Animosity, make a Psychology Test (page 183). On a failure, it must attack the target socially or physically, as appropriate, gaining +1 SL on Fellowship based Tests to oppose or disparage them. See page 183 for full Animosity rules.

traits.name: Belligerent
traits.text: The creature loves to win a fight. As long as they possess Momentum, they are immune to Fear.

traits.name: Bestial
traits.text: The creature has no rational thought or language. It shies away from fire and gains a Broken Condition if struck and wounded by it. In defence, it only uses the Dodge Skill. If it loses more than half its Wounds, it will attempt to Flee unless protecting its young or cornered, or unless it has the Territorial Trait. If so, it enters Frenzy (see page 184).

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: The creature may lose Momentum to make a Free Attack. The Damage equals Rating and includes their Strength Bonus already. Free Attack - Weapon Skill or Ballistic Skill attack that does not use your Action on your Turn.

traits.name: Blessed
traits.text: The creature can enact Blessings, the relevant deity is indicated in parentheses. A creature with this Trait has a Pray Skill at Fel + 10 (or more at the GM’s discretion).

traits.name: Bounce
traits.text: The creature can bounce high, perhaps with powerful limbs, magic, or stubby wings. When Charging, Leaping, or Sprinting, they double their Movement Attribute and can ignore all intervening terrain and creatures as they leap over them.

traits.name: Breath
traits.text: The creature’s breath is a powerful weapon. As a ranged attack, they can activate their Breath as a Free Attack, targeting 1 creature they can see within 20 + Toughness Bonus yards and all creatures within SB yards of that target. The attacker makes an Opposed Ballistic Skill/Dodge Test against all targets (the attacker's single roll Opposed by each individual target). If a creature without a BS makes a Breath Attack, count it as having a BS of 30. Losing targets take Rating Damage. Further, if the Trait has any of the following Types in parentheses, apply the associated rules. 0 Acid: Inflicts Damage of TB +4. All weapons and armour carried by the targets suffer 1 Damage. 0 Cold: Inflicts Damage of SB +2. Targets gain a Fatigued Condition; until they lose the Condition, their weapons gain the Slow Flaw. 0 Electricity: Inflicts Damage of SB +2. Damage ignores metal armour. Targets gain a Stunned Condition. 0 Fire: Inflicts Damage of SB +3. Targets gain an Ablaze Condition. 0 Poison: Inflicts Damage of TB +2. Targets gain a Poisoned Condition. 0 Smoke: The area fills with smoke, blocking line of sight and causing Suffocation (page 169) for Toughness Bonus Rounds. The creature is immune to their own Breath. This attack is Magical.

traits.name: Champion
traits.text: The creature is an extraordinarily skilled warrior. If they win an Opposed Test when defending in melee combat, they can cause Damage just as if they were the attacker.

traits.name: Chill Grasp
traits.text: The creature’s touch chills their enemies’ souls. If they lose Momentum, then for their Action, they can attempt an Opposed Weapon Skill/Dodge or Melee Test. If they win, the target loses 1d10 + SL Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. This attack is Magical.

traits.name: Cold-blooded
traits.text: The creature is cold-blooded and slow to react. They gain Advantage to Cool Tests. If they gain the Surprised Condition, this Condition is not lost the first time it should be (typically at the end of the Round or if they are attacked).

traits.name: Constrictor
traits.text: The creature can squeeze and crush their prey. Any successful hit gives the target an Entangled Condition. The creature may then enter a Grapple if they wish (see page 167).

traits.name: Construct
traits.text: The creature is a construct of magic, quite mindless, and bound together with enchantments. It has no Intelligence, Willpower, or Fellowship Characteristics, and need never Test them. If it is ever called upon to Test based on Willpower, use Toughness instead. If it has no spellcaster controlling it, or does not possess the Territorial Trait, it wanders mindlessly. For the purpose of calculating its Wounds, use its Strength Bonus whenever Willpower Bonus is required. All its attacks are Magical.

traits.name: Corrosive Blood
traits.text: The creature’s blood is corrosive. Every time they are wounded, blood splashes free and all targets Engaged with them take 1d10 Damage (roll once and apply to all targets).

traits.name: Corruption
traits.text: The creature is tainted by Chaos, or perhaps suffused with Dark Magics. They are a Corrupting Influence with a Strength marked in parentheses. See page 187.

traits.name: Dark Vision
traits.text: The creature can see in the dark as if it were daylight.

traits.name: Daemonic
traits.text: The creature’s essence is raw magic, and unholy ichor pumps through what passes for their veins. Daemonic creatures do not require the normal prerequisites for life such as food, water, air, and so on. All their attacks are Magical. Roll 1d10 after any blow is received, if the creature rolls Rating or higher, the blow is ignored, even if it is a Critical. They may not use this ability to ignore Magical blows such as those caused by creatures with the Magical Trait or weapons with the Magical Quality. Should the creature be reduced to 0 Wounds, their soul returns to the Realms of Chaos immediately, removing them from play.

traits.name: Disease
traits.text: The creature carries the disease listed, though whether they suffer from the disease is up to the GM. Others will have to Test as appropriate for Contraction (see page 179).

traits.name: Distracting
traits.text: The creature distracts or confuses foes, possibly exuding a soporific musk or nauseating reek, or through its bizarre and horrifying appearance. All living targets within a number of yards equal to the creature’s Toughness Bonus suffer a -2 SL penalty to all Tests. A target can only suffer this penalty once, no matter how many Distracting foes there are.

traits.name: Ethereal
traits.text: The creature’s form is insubstantial, allowing them to pass through solid objects. They can only be harmed by Magical attacks and all their attacks are Magical.

traits.name: Fear
traits.text: The creature causes supernatural Fear in other creatures. Opponents must make an Extended Psychology Test (page 183). Until they have accumulated more SL than the creature’s Fear Rating (1, if not stated), they cannot gain Momentum, and melee attacks against them benefit from Advantage. See page 183 for Fear rules.

traits.name: Fly
traits.text: As the creature’s Move, they can fly up to Rating yards. When flying, they ignore all intervening terrain, obstacles, or creatures. At the end of the move, they decide whether they have landed or are still flying. They can use this move to Charge. If they start their turn flying, they must choose to Fly for their Move. If they cannot do this, the GM decides how far the creature falls (see page 169). When targeting them, measure horizontal distance as normal, then increase range by 1 step. So, a Long Range shot would become Extreme Range, and if they were at Extreme Range, they could not be shot at all. When flying, they suffer a -20 penalty to Ranged Attacks as they swoop and wheel in the sky.

traits.name: Frenzy
traits.text: The creature may make a Willpower Test to enter a Frenzy (page 184). While Frenzied, they are immune to Psychology, cannot flee or retreat, must attack the nearest visible enemy, gain a Free Attack each Round, +1 Damage, and may only attack or move to attack. Frenzy ends when no enemies remain in sight, or if the creature becomes Stunned or Unconscious. Afterwards, they gain a Fatigued Condition.

traits.name: Ghostly Howl
traits.text: The creature can emit a hideous scream, capable of killing those who hear it. Once per turn, this creature can lose their Momentum to unleash a howl as a Free Attack. All living targets within a number of yards equal to the creature’s Strength who can hear it immediately gain 3 Deafened Conditions and suffer 1d10 Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Those affected must also pass an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or gain a Broken Condition. This attack is Magical.

traits.name: Grim
traits.text: The creature is incredibly lethal, able to quickly gain the upper hand over almost any opponent. At the end of its turn, if the creature does not have Momentum (page 167), it gains it.

traits.name: Hatred
traits.text: When the creature encounters the Target, they must make a Psychology Test (page 183). On a failure, they become subject to Hatred. While Hatred lasts, they must attack the hated foe by the fastest and most deadly means possible, gain +1 SL on Melee and Ranged Tests against them, and are immune to Intimidate and Fear (but not Terror) caused by the Target. See page 184 for full Hatred rules.

traits.name: Horns
traits.text: The creature has horns or some other sharp appendage (if their Horns Trait represents a different feature, it will be noted in parentheses). When the creature charges into combat, they may make a Free Attack with their Horns, with a Damage of SB +4.

traits.name: Hungry
traits.text: The creature is always hungry for fresh meat. If they kill or incapacitate a living opponent (or encounter a fresh body), they must pass an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or feast, losing their next Move and Action.

traits.name: Immune to Psychology
traits.text: Whether brave, stupid, or just caught up in the moment, the creature is utterly stoic. They ignore the Psychology rules (see page 183).

traits.name: Immunity
traits.text: The creature is completely immune to a certain type of harm, such as poison, magic, or electricity. All harm of that type, including from a Critical Wound, is ignored.

traits.name: Infected
traits.text: The creature, or their weapon, carries a nasty infection. If they cause a living opponent to lose Wounds, the opponent must pass an Easy (+4 SL) Endurance Test or contract a Festering Wound (see page 180).

traits.name: Infestation
traits.text: The creature’s hide is infested with biting fleas or similar. All opponents suffer a penalty of -1 SL to hit them in melee combat as the parasites distract and overwhelm them.

traits.name: Many Heads
traits.text: The creature has more than one head. If a Critical Wound affecting the head stuns, kills, or renders the creature unconscious it will only affect the creature once all the heads are either disabled or affected to a similar degree. If the creature has the Bite, Horns, or Tongue Traits it can make a number of Free Attacks equal to the number of healthy heads. The creature benefits from +2 SL to Perception Tests whilst it has at least two healthy heads.

traits.name: Mark of Chaos
traits.text: One of the dark powers has marked this creature with a physical brand, proclaiming it one of their favoured servants. The exact effects of this mark depend on which of the Chaos gods bestowed the Mark. Khorne: The creature benefits from the Frenzy Talent. This creature gains the Etiquette (Followers of Khorne) Talent and is subject to Animosity towards overt followers of Slaanesh. The creature is also subject to Animosity by followers of Slaanesh, so long as the Mark of Khorne is visible. The Character may not use the Language (Magick) or Channelling skills unless it is to dispel a spell. Additionally, they may purchase the following Talents as if they were Career Advances for the normal XP costs: Berserk Charge, Combat Aware, Combat Reflexes, Furious Assault, Implacable, Magic Resistance, Resistance (Magic), Resolute, Strike Mighty Blow, Warrior Born. Nurgle: The creature benefits from a bonus of +10 to its Toughness. This creature gains the Etiquette (Followers of Nurgle) Talent and is subject to Animosity towards overt followers of Tzeentch. The creature is also subject to Animosity by followers of Tzeentch, so long as the Mark of Nurgle is visible. Additionally they may purchase the following Talents as if they were Career Advances for the normal XP costs: Frightening, Hardy, Implacable, Iron Jaw, Menacing, Resistance (Poison), Resistance (Disease), Robust, Tenacious, and Very Resilient. Slaanesh: The creature gains the Fearless (Everything) Talent. This creature gains the Etiquette (Followers of Slaanesh) Talent and is subject to Animosity towards overt followers of Khorne. The creature is also subject to Animosity by followers of Khorne, so long as the Mark of Slaanesh is visible. Additionally, they may purchase the following Talents as if they were Career Advances for the normal XP costs: Attractive, Blather, Careful Strike, Combat Master, Gregarious, Inspiring, Lightning Reflexes, Nimblefingered, Resistant (Poison), and Sharp. Tzeentch: This creature gains 1d10/3 Mutations (rounding up), alternating between Mental and Physical Mutations. This creature gains Etiquette (Followers of Tzeentch), and is subject to Animosity towards overt followers of Nurgle. The creature is also subject to Animosity by followers of Nurgle, so long as the Mark of Tzeentch can be seen. Additionally, this creature may purchase the following Talents as if they were Career Advances: Aethyric Attunement, Arcane Magic (Any), Chaos Magic (Tzeentch), Fast Hands, Instinctive Diction, Magical Sense, Petty Magic, Second Sight, War Wizard, and Witch! for the normal XP costs.

traits.name: Magical
traits.text: The creature is wreathed in magic. Their attacks count as Magical, and they can harm creatures only susceptible to Magical attacks.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.text: The creature is resistant to magic. Any Casting Test to cast a Spell that would affect them suffers -3 SL. No creature with this Trait may possess the Channelling Skill or the Arcane Magic, Bless, Chaos Magic, Invoke, Petty Magic, or Witch! Talents, and vice versa.

traits.name: Mental Corruption
traits.text: The creature has Chaos on the mind. Roll on the Mental Corruption Table found on page 189.

traits.name: Miracles
traits.text: The creature can enact Miracles; the relevant deity is indicated in parentheses. A creature with this Trait has a Pray Skill at Fel + 10 (or more at the GM’s discretion).

traits.name: Mutation
traits.text: The creature bears a Mutation. Roll on the Physical Corruption Table found on page 189.

traits.name: Night Vision
traits.text: The creature can see very well in natural darkness. They can see clearly in such darkness for 20 yards and can extend the effective illumination distance of any light sources by a further 20 yards.

traits.name: Painless
traits.text: The creature is impervious to pain. All non-amputation penalties suffered from Critical Wounds are ignored, although Conditions are suffered as normal.

traits.name: Petrifying Gaze
traits.text: The creature’s gaze can turn flesh to stone. As an Action, the creature may lose its Momentum to unleash its petrifying gaze against one living target it can see. The creature makes a Ballistic Skill Test, opposed by the target’s Initiative. If the creature wins, it inflicts a Stunned Condition, and one more for each SL after the first. If they win by 6+ SL, the target is permanently turned to stone. If the target is a spellcaster, they can oppose the Test with Language (Magick) instead of Initiative.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.text: The creature can heal at an extraordinary rate, even regrowing severed parts. At the start of each Round, if they have more than 0 Wounds remaining, they automatically regenerate 1d10 Wounds. If they have 0 Wounds remaining, they regenerate a single Wound on a 1d10 roll of 8+. If they ever roll a 10 for regenerating, they also fully regenerate a Critical Wound, losing all penalties and Conditions associated with it. Any Wounds or Critical Wounds caused by fire may not be regenerated.

traits.name: Size
traits.text:
This Trait represents creatures whose size differs from the game standard (i.e. roughly human-sized). There are five steps of Size, ranging from Tiny to Monstrous. Size Examples Butterfly, Mouse, Pigeon, Cat, Hawk, Tiny Human Infant Giant Rat, Halfling, Human Child, Average Dwarf, Elf, Human Large Horse, Ogre, Troll Enormous Griffon, Wyvern, Manticore Monstrous Dragon, Giant, Greater Daemon Size Combat Modifiers Large creatures do more Damage when they land a hit. These modifiers don’t apply to Ranged Attacks or extra attacks. NPC profiles already include these modifiers. 
• Small: Damage as normal 
• Average: Damage as normal 
• Large: Damage as normal plus additional SB Damage 
• Enormous: Damage as normal plus additional SB Damage 
• Monstrous: Damage as normal plus additional (2 x SB) Damage Defending Against Big Creatures When fighting a creature of larger size, you suffer a penalty of -2 SL when using Melee to defend in an Opposed Test. It is better to dodge a giant swinging a tree trunk than try to parry it! Fear Agressive creatures cause Fear in those smaller than them. Moving in Combat Creatures ignore the need to Disengage from melee combat with smaller combatants. Opposed Strength During Opposed Strength Tests (and similar), if one creature is 2 or more Size steps larger, they win automatically. If one creature is 1 Size step larger, the smaller creature must score a Critical to contest the roll. If they do, SL are compared as normal. All other results mean the larger creature wins. Outnumbering Larger Creatures Larger creatures count as several creatures for the sake of working out if they are outnumbered in combat. 
• Small: Counts as 1 creature 
• Average: Counts as 1 creature 
• Large: Counts as 2 creatures 
• Enormous: Counts as 3 creatures 
• Monstrous: Counts as 4 creatures So, you would need 4 Size (Average) creatures to outnumber a Size (Large) creature by 2 to 1, or 3 Size (Large) creatures to outnumber a Size (Monstrous) creature by 2 to 1. Conversely, for the sake of larger opponents being daunting enough, they do not themselves count as multiple opponents when working out if they receive a bonus for outnumbering themselves. 2 Size (Large) Ogres outnumber 1 Size (Average) Human 2 to 1, not 4 to 1. Creatures that are larger than their opponents may lose Momentum to make one Stomp as a Free Attack, kicking downwards or otherwise bashing smaller opponents out of the way. This attack has a Damage equal to their Strength Bonus and uses Melee (Brawling). Larger creatures have more Wounds: Size Wounds Small 2 × Toughness Bonus Strength Bonus + (2 × Toughness Average Bonus) + Willpower Bonus (Strength Bonus + (2 × Toughness Large Bonus) + Willpower Bonus) × 2 (Strength Bonus + (2 × Toughness Enormous Bonus) + Willpower Bonus) × 4 (Strength Bonus + (2 × Toughness Monstrous Bonus) + Willpower Bonus) × 8 ADJUSTING A CREATURE’S SIZE if you wish to use Size to make a creature bigger then increase Strength and Toughness by +10 and reduce Agility by -5 per step of size you increase the creature. reverse this if you wish to make a creature smaller. Example: The Giant Spider described in the Bestiary is Size (Small) with a Strength of 15, Toughness of 25, and an Agility of 35. If it were made Size (Large) it would have a Strength of 35, Toughness of 45, and Agility of 25. Its Wounds would increase to 26, its fangs would inflict +5 Damage and its Bite would increase to +6 Damage.

traits.name: Skittish
traits.text: The creature is scared by spectacular visible effects of magic or noises such as thunderclaps or explosions. If such occurs, they receive +3 Broken Conditions.

traits.name: Spellcaster
traits.text: The creature can cast spells; the specific Lore(s) of Magic are indicated in parentheses. Add the Spellcaster or Spellcaster Lord template or, if that wouldn’t be appropriate, add Channelling (Choose a Wind) (WP +10) and Language (Magick) (Int + 10) as if they were Basic Skills. The GM may increase the numbers of skills if they deem it appropriate.

traits.name: Sprinter
traits.text: The creature has a long stride, perhaps because it is a quadruped or has especially long legs. Multiply Run Movement by 1.5 when Running.

traits.name: Stealthy
traits.text: The creature is especially stealthy. They are granted the Stealth (Rural) Skill at Ag +10. This number may be increased at the GM’s discretion.

traits.name: Striding Gait
traits.text: The creature is at home in the listed terrain. They suffer no penalties for moving through the listed terrain and add +1 SL to Athletics and Stealth Tests in the listed terrain.

traits.name: Stupid
traits.text: While not devoid of self-awareness (and so lacking the Bestial Trait), the creature is stupid. If they are near any allies without the Stupid Trait, they guide them and nothing happens. Otherwise, they must pass an Easy (+4 SL) Intelligence Test at the start of each Round or become very confused. Should this occur, they will drool, perhaps sitting down or picking their nose, doing little of use, losing both their Move and Action for that Turn.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.text: Swarms are large numbers of the same creature acting as one. The swarm counts as a single creature that ignores the Psychology rules (see page 183), and can ignore the Engaged rules when using its Move. All opponents Engaged with a Swarm automatically lose 1 Wound at the end of every Round as the Swarm overwhelms anything close. The Swarm has five times the Wounds of a normal example of the creature and gains +10 Weapon Skill. Any attempts to shoot the Swarm gain a +40 bonus to hit. Swarms ignore all the Size Creature Trait rules.

traits.name: Tail
traits.text: The creature’s tail is capable of sweeping foes from their feet. They may lose Momentum to make a Free Attack that does SB +2 Damage. Smaller-Size targets that suffer any Wounds from the attack also gain the Prone Condition.

traits.name: Tentacles
traits.text: The creature has a number of tentacles equal to #. They gain one Free Attack per tentacle. Each tentacle’s attack does Damage of SB +0. If they cause Damage, they can also give their opponent an Entangled Condition, which will initiate a Grapple between the target and that tentacle. If a tentacle is Grappling, use the tentacle’s Free Attack to resolve that Grapple, not the creature’s Action (see page 167).

traits.name: Territorial
traits.text: This creature is protective of a particular area or location. They will fight to the death to protect it and will not normally pursue enemies if they flee this area.

traits.name: Terror
traits.text: The creature supernaturally causes bone-chilling Terror. When first encountering the creature, opponents must make a Psychology Test (page 183). On a failure, opponents gain Broken Conditions equal to the Terror Rating, plus 1 for each negative SL. Regardless of the result, it also causes Fear (page 183) with an equal Fear Rating.

traits.name: Tongue
traits.text: The creature’s prehensile tongue can wrap itself around prey, dragging it to a grisly end. They may lose Momentum to make a Free Attack. This is a Ranged Attack that does Damage of SB +0. It is up to the GM to decide on the range, though a default is 3 yards for creatures of Size (Small to Large) and 12 yards for larger creatures. If the attack hits, the target receives 1 Entangled Condition and, if a smaller Size, is dragged towards the creature, and is Engaged in melee combat. The creature can then choose whether to release the target, perform a Free Attack using its Weapon Trait, or keep the target wrapped in their tongue, initiating a Grapple (see page 167).

traits.name: Tracker
traits.text: Trackers are adept at following their prey, generally through scent or hearing. The creature is granted the Track Skill at Int +10. This number may be increased at the GM’s discretion.

traits.name: Trained
traits.text: This Trait represents animals that have been trained through the Animal Training Skill. The skills the animal knows are marked in the parentheses. Feel free to create your own Trained skills. Broken: The animal is trained to ignore its Bestial Trait. It receives +2d10 Fellowship. Drive: The animal is trained to pull a coach, cart, plough, buggy, or similar. Entertain: The animal is trained to entertain others. It adds a +10 bonus to appropriate Entertain, Perform, or Play Tests. Fetch: The animal is trained to fetch. This is normally reserved for dogs and similar. Guard: The animal is trained to stay in one place or prowl around as a guard, granting it the Territorial Trait. Home: The animal is trained to return home if it is released or lost. Magic: The animal is trained to ignore Skittish when it comes to magic, which is required for most mounts used by spellcasters. Mount: The animal accepts a rider. Some creatures are especially belligerent, and will not accept a rider without the correct skill. For example, to ride a griffon, you need the Ride (Griffon) Skill. War: The animal is trained for war, gaining +10 Weapon Skill. It can also ignore Skittish for loud noises.

traits.name: Undead
traits.text: The undead are neither living nor dead, meaning they are not reliant on the usual prerequisites for life such as air, food, water, and so on. This Trait most commonly comes into use when spells, Miracles, or other abilities affect Undead only.

traits.name: Unstable
traits.text: The creature’s corpus is maintained by foul magics that are inherently unstable in the material realm. Whenever they end a Round Engaged with any opponents who possess Momentum when they do not, the creature is driven back, and the magics holding them together weaken and the creature loses 2 Wounds. If the creature ever reaches 0 Wounds, the magics holding them in place collapse, and they are destroyed or driven back from whence they came.

traits.name: Vampiric
traits.text: The creature feeds on blood and draws great physical strength from this act. Whenever they perform a successful Bite attack against an appropriate opponent, they heal as many Wounds as the opponent loses. Drinking blood in this way is the only way they can heal.

traits.name: Venom
traits.text: The creature’s attacks are poisoned or envenomed. When they cause Wounds, their opponent gains a Poisoned Condition. Some poisons are more potent than others, and the listed Difficulty should apply to Tests made to recover from the Poisoned Condition. See page 186.

traits.name: Vomit
traits.text: Under duress, the creature can spew a stream of corrosive spew, dowsing their opponents in foul, semi-digested filth. If the creature starts their Turn engaged in combat, they can give up their Move and Action to activate their Vomit. The attacker performs an Opposed Ballistic Skill/Dodge Test against all targets within 2 yards (the attacker’s single roll opposed by each individual target). The Test is Easy (+4 SL) for the vomiting creature, due to the close range, and Challenging (+0 SL) for opponents. All losing targets suffer a hit with TB +4 Damage and receive a Stunned condition. All weapons and armour carried by affected targets suffer 1 Damage as stomach acid corrodes them away. A creature may only Vomit once every 12 hours.

traits.name: Ward
traits.text: Perhaps because they are magical, wear a special talisman, or are just plain lucky, some blows just seem to miss. Roll 1d10 after any blow is received: if the roll is Rating or higher, the blow is ignored, even if it is a Critical.

traits.name: Wallcrawler
traits.text: The creature can effortlessly scale vertical surfaces and even traverse ceilings, ready to drop on unwary prey. They move at full Movement across any appropriate surface and automatically pass all Climb Tests.

traits.name: Web
traits.text: The creature can create webbing to trap unwary foes. Whenever they successfully hit, opponents gain 1 Entangled Condition, with a Strength of the Rating given. See page 186.

traits.name: Vigor Mortis
traits.text: Any Undead within 8 of the Corpse Cart are no longer subject to Unstable; the Cart itself remains subject to it. Necromancy spells cast within 8 receive +20. These effects end when the Cart is destroyed.

traits.name: Balefire Brazier
traits.text: Replaces the normal Necromancy casting benefit of Vigor Mortis: all Lore (Magic) checks within 8 suffer −20. The protection of nearby Undead from Unstable remains.

traits.name: Arboreal
traits.text: Add the creature's Agility Bonus in SL to Stealth and Climb Tests in woodlands.

traits.name: Die Hard
traits.text: All Critical Wounds can be healed. For Toughness Bonus Rounds after death, at the start of each Round make a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test. On success, return to life with 1 Wound.
traits.adaptation: User-supplied older-edition definition retained; no direct Fifth Edition equivalent.

traits.name: Prejudice
traits.text: Printed Prejudice (Thin People); no Fifth Edition mechanical definition is supplied. This entry is a reference only, without invented Test modifiers.

traits.name: Corrupting Vomit
traits.text: Those hit by a Chaos Troll’s vomit risk exposure to Corruption (Moderate).

traits.name: Rotten Regeneration
traits.text: Use core Regeneration, but the Wounds restored are 1d10 divided by 2, rounded down (Tribes and Tribulations p. 88).

traits.name: Bileful Vomit
traits.text: The Troll’s Vomit follows core Stream of Corruption: CN: 9 Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant Your maw distends horrifically before you vomit forth a foul stream of diseased filth and horror. Immediately make an Unopposed Acid- and Poison-type Breath attack (see page 357). It counts as a magic missile with a Damage equal to your Toughness Bonus, and it ignores Armour Points. Further, any targets that take more than their TB in Wounds must pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test or contract Blood Rot (see page 179).

traits.name: That’s No Mound
traits.text: The Troll has Stealthy only while it has not moved or taken an Action.

traits.name: Sated
traits.text: After consuming a creature of Average Size or larger in peace, the Hungry Troll template no longer applies.

traits.name: Starving
traits.text: If the Hungry Troll does not eat within 24 hours it begins to suffer Starvation.

traits.name: Water Wise
traits.text: While within a body of water, the River Troll Hag does not suffer from Stupid. Stupid otherwise remains active.

traits.name: Purple Skullback Bite
traits.text: A creature wounded and Poisoned by this bite takes an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test or gains 1 Corruption point. A Forest Goblin Shaman still takes damage and poison, but for 2d10 hours gains a printed +2d10 bonus to Channelling and Language (Magick), and may reroll Waaagh! Miscast results. Situational bonuses are not added permanently.
traits.adaptation: Printed Average (+20) uses core Average (+2 SL); current Venom inflicts Poisoned on Wounds without an avoidance Test.

traits.name: Lure of the Lurkerfish
traits.text: The gently oscillating blue- green lights seen by the riverbank at dusk and dawn are sometimes mistaken for fireflies. Any Character passing a Hard (−2 SL) Lore (Riverways) Test will know that these are likely to be the lures of Lurkerfish. Those who fail the Lore Test must make an Easy (+4 SL) Cool Test or become beguiled by the sight and unable to perform any action except moving towards the light — effectively acquiring the Unconscious Condition.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

traits.name: Slimy
traits.text: Latch-eels can produce a surprising quantity of slime, in or out of the water. If a Latch-eel is ever Grappled by an opponent, it may make a Toughness Test. If it succeeds, it produces a clump of slime, benefiting from +4 SL to subsequent Tests to break free. The opponent must make a Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics Test. Failure means that slime has covered their face, and the opponent must either release the Latch-eel or start to suffer suffocation (WFRP, page 181).

traits.name: Love the Light
traits.text: Daggerfish are attracted to light. Attempts to use fire to deter them only encourages them further. Whilst they possess the Bestial trait, they do not shy from fire or take Broken Conditions from being struck by flaming attacks.

traits.name: Immersion
traits.text: The Sea Elemental may attempt to immerse its opponents by making a Grapple. If the Sea Elemental inflicts an Entangled Condition on its opponent, it draws them into its own body. The immersed character suffers from Suffocation as detailed on WFRP, page 181. They may attempt to escape by freeing themselves from the Entangled Condition as if they were Grappled by the Sea Elemental, making Opposed Strength Tests against its Strength of 59 to break free. However, the Sea Elemental does not need to actively maintain the Grapple — it may act as if the immersed character were not there and does not count as being Engaged.

traits.name: Fire Resistant
traits.text: Sea Elementals never suffer from Ablaze Conditions.

traits.name: Mindless Spellcaster
traits.text: Sea Elementals may use their Strength Characteristic for the purpose of casting spells and channelling.

traits.name: Boat Crusher
traits.text: The Gargantuan may attempt to constrict a vessel of Size Large or smaller. To constrict a vessel, it must spend one turn wrapping itself about the vessel for every 10 points of Size the vessel possesses. Once the vessel is wrapped up, the Gargantuan starts to squeeze — making an Extended Opposed Strength Test against the boat’s Toughness. Once the SL reaches the boat’s Wounds, the boat shatters, reduced to a mass of flotsam. During this time, the boat’s crew may attack the Gargantuan or attempt to lever it from the boat. Attacks that inflict more than 7 Wounds may cause the Gargantuan to let go if it fails a subsequent Average (+2 SL) Cool Test. Levering the Gargantuan requires making an Opposed Strength Test against the creature. A result of 0 to 4 SL prevents it from squeezing the boat that turn, and a result of 5 SL or more forces it to release the boat.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

traits.name: Electrical Discharge
traits.text: If the creature successfully Grapples an opponent, then at the start of its subsequent turns, the creature can spend 1 Momentum to deliver an electric shock to the Grappled character. The electrical discharge inflicts a hit of 10 Damage which ignores non- magical metal armour. Any Character taking Wounds from the electrical attack must also pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance Test or suffer a Stunned Condition. The Gargantuan cannot make electrical attacks with impunity. Each time it uses the attack, it must make an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test. Failure indicates that it suffers a Fatigued Condition. Whilst the Gargantuan is under the effects of a Fatigued Condition, electrical discharge attacks only inflict Damage 6 hits which ignore non-magical metal armour. The Gargantuan may also discharge electricity when it has Grappled a boat. This does no damage against the boat, but the crew all receive a jolt, suffering a Damage 6 hit (reduced to a Damage 3 hit if the Gargantuan has a Fatigued Condition).
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers. Printed Advantage uses Momentum.

traits.name: Whale Bane
traits.text: All Fanged Maw attacks have core Venom (Difficult −1 SL recovery): causing Wounds inflicts Poisoned; the Difficulty applies to recovery.
traits.adaptation: Uses full Fifth Edition Venom rather than the older on-hit interpretation.

traits.name: Syreen’s Call
traits.text: As an action the Syreen may sing its luring song. Characters within a number of yards equal to the Syreen’s Initiative must make an Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test or become beguiled by the call and unable to perform any action except moving towards the Syreen — effectively acquiring the Unconscious Condition.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

traits.name: Resistant to Cold
traits.text: Any weapon, spell, or effect that inflicts damage or impairment due to cold will likely have a reduced impact on an Orb Leviathan. It may make an Endurance Test to ignore any ill effects from cold and ice.

traits.name: Lure of the Leviathan
traits.text: The first sign of an approaching attack by an Orb Leviathan is a lambent yellow light drifting slowly underwater. Any Character passing a Hard (−2 SL) Lore (Oceans) Test will have heard about the lure of the Orb Leviathan, and may look away before it takes effect. Those who fail the Lore Test must succeed on an Easy (+4 SL) Cool Test or acquire the Stunned Condition.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty uses current SL modifiers.

traits.name: Devastating Assault
traits.text: When a Black Leviathan charges a ship, it causes a collision with a CR of 50.

traits.name: On a Different Scale
traits.text: The Black Leiviathan possesses the Bestial Trait and can be scared by fire. However, guttering torches are too small to attract its notice, let alone scare it. To benefit from the frightening qualities of fire, the blaze must be the size and intensity of a large bonfire; anything less isn’t going to concern the Black Leviathan. When considering the psychological impact of other sources of Fear and Terror, the GM should consider that unless the source is something the Black Leviathan should respect in terms of size, it is unlikely to bother the beast. Unearthly as Daemonettes, Zombies, and wizards with flaming heads may be, the Black Leviathan regards them all as fish food.

traits.name: Marine Creature
traits.text: The creature is at home in the ocean and unsuited to life on land. Its printed profile assumes an aquatic environment and it moves its full Movement in water. Out of water, Movement drops to 1 and all its Tests suffer −2 SL. It must be regularly doused with water or begin to suffocate (core Suffocation).

traits.name: Telepathy
traits.text: The creature can communicate without words, using the power of its mind to transmit and read thoughts. If the subject wants to resist their thoughts being read, they must pass an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Chameleon
traits.text: The creature can change colour to blend into its surroundings, which makes it very hard to see. Perception Tests to spot the creature suffer a –4 SL penalty, reduced to –2 if the creature is moving. Shooting at the creature suffers a –2 SL penalty to the Ranged Test.

traits.name: Flammable
traits.text: Many plants and some animals are particularly susceptible to damage caused by heat and flame. Any Tests the creature makes to avoid suffering an Ablaze Condition suffer a penalty of –20. Furthermore, creatures with the Flammable Trait suffer twice as many Wounds as they otherwise would from Ablaze Conditions.

traits.name: Stationary Attacker
traits.text: Many plants and simple invertebrates are not fully mobile and active the way that opponents in Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay are normally considered to be. Instead, they behave more like traps or environmental hazards than they do creatures. Plants such as Impaling Spikethorn, or sessile creatures such as Pallid Blindwyrms are examples of stationary attackers. Creatures with the Stationary Attacker Trait have the Immunity to Psychology Trait. They occupy a particular location, and whilst they are hostile towards suitable prey that blunder into that location, they are not able to pursue them or manoeuvre around them. They may not take Charge, Flee, Leap, Run, or Climb Actions, or any other actions besides those which are associated with their attacks and Traits. However, if an unsuspecting target moves within reach of a creature with the Stationary Attacker Trait, that creature counts as Engaged with them, and may spring an attack, inflicting the Surprised Condition on the target as it does so. The reach of a Stationary Attacker depends on its Size. Usually, Stationary Attackers blend in with the undergrowth, appearing unassuming until they make their attacks. For a Character to recognise the threat, they must first pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Perception Test to notice the presence of the Stationary Attacker, followed by a suitable Lore Test to identify it. If either test is failed, the Character does not recognise the threat. Reach: Tiny/Little Very Short; Small Short; Average Medium; Large Long; Enormous Very Long; Monstrous Massive.

traits.name: Auger and Scryer
traits.text: GMs with access to Altdorf: Crown of the Empire or Winds of Magic may make use of the Psychometry and Augury rules in relation to the Slann. They are also capable of using the Psychometry Skill as if it were a Basic Skill and may ignore the usual prohibition on being both a magician and a Scryer.

traits.name: Contemplation
traits.text: Slann often appear distant and detached. They are not lacking in awareness, but their contemplations into distant events or future likelihoods often take priority over their appreciation of the here and now. When a Slann is not being interacted with, they are likely to become lost in contemplation. Should circumstances in the vicinity of the Slann change, the Slann should make a Difficult (−1 SL) Perception Test to see if they realise what is going on. CONTEMPLATION TABLE SL Result +2 or More Alive to the Moment. The Slann is alert and may react to happenings in their surroundings with no penalty. 0 to +1 Detached. The Slann is subject to distraction but has at least some appreciation of what is occurring in their vicinity. They suffer from the Stupid Creature Trait for the rest of the encounter, and then either become fully alert or drift back into meditation depending on the circumstances. –0 to –3 Thought Fog. The Slann is dimly aware of goings on around them. They suffer from two Fatigued Conditions. On their turn they can either Move or take an Action, but not both. –4 or less Lost in Thought. The Slann has no awareness of what is going on around them and does not react to actions taken by nearby characters. Unresponsive Slann may be forced to take their Perception Test again. If loud noises, bright lights, or other stimuli are used to alert the Slann, they may Test again with a Challenging (+0 SL) Perception Test to see if they are stirred into awareness. If the Slann is assailed with weapons or magic, this becomes an Easy (+4 SL) Perception Test. Also note that because of their Telepathy rule, a Slann who is alerted to dangers by another Slann or a Skink magic- user will become Alive to the Moment.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulties use core Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Knack for Total Power
traits.text: These ancient Slann are gifted magicians who can summon overwhelming magical energies where lesser spellcasters might struggle. Such Slann count as scoring a Critical on their successful Casting Tests when rolling a double or when their roll includes a ‘0’ on the units die. Whilst in Lustria, they may also reroll any Tests to perceive the Winds of Magic.

traits.name: Master of Magical Mishaps
traits.text: Experienced Slann rarely make mistakes when casting spells. If such a Slann suffers a Major Miscast, it becomes a Minor Miscast instead. This rule does not apply if the Slann is casting a spell through another spellcaster using their Telepathy rule.

traits.name: Emergency Teleportation
traits.text: Slann are routinely provided with protective amulets that transport them away from harm if they face the risk of injury and death. Whenever a Slann is reduced to 10 Wounds or less, or receives a Critical Wound resulting in broken bones, torn muscles, or worse, they can immediately take a free action to cast the Arcane Spell Teleport (WFRP, page 244). If the spell is cast successfully, the Slann is immediately transported to the star chamber within a pyramid-temple of the nearest temple-city (or a neighbouring temple-city if that star chamber is not safe). It is plausible that a wizard of another species could adapt such amulets to their own use, but the vast energies of the Geomantic Web are involved in this teleportation, and only the Slann have been known to use them and survive the experience.

traits.name: Relic Priest
traits.text: Relic Priests are the mummified remains of truly ancient Slann. The profile given is for the spirit form of such priests, which must remain within Willpower Bonus yards of their bodies. The bodies possess the same number of Wounds as the spirits. Destroying the body will destroy the spirit with it. Damage to either the body or the spirit may trigger the Emergency Teleportation rule. The spirit may possess its body and use it to direct a palanquin, but other than this, the body itself may not move or take actions. The spirit may cast a spell for either of its actions, meaning it may cast up to two spells per turn if it does not move or take other actions. The body of the Relic Priest counts as having the Prone Condition at all times. The spirit may have some meagre ability to fight in melee, though this is just for the purpose of determining defence against attacks; it cannot inflict damage of its own.

traits.name: Slann Telepathy
traits.text: The Slann are in constant contact with each other and their favoured servants via telepathic communication. A Slann may share their thoughts with others in their network, which is defined as those Slann and Skink Priests within Willpower Yards, and, provided that the Slann is within Willpower Yards of a flow of energy in the Geomantic Web, any other Slann within Willpower Yards of a similar flow of energy. As their Action or Move, a Slann may concentrate on telepathic communication by passing a Challenging (+0 SL) Intelligence Test. If this Test is passed, the Slann may perform one of the following Actions. 0 Share Intelligence: The Slann may ask questions of, and provide answers to, another within their network. This is not an exact process, as Slann are alien in their thinking and given to pondering tangential thoughts even when pressed. However, in a single Turn, a Slann could have the equivalent of a five minute conversation in this manner. 0 Cast a Spell: A Slann may seize the consciousness of a Skink Priest in their network for the purpose of casting a spell. The Slann may use their own Characteristics, Skills, and Talents when casting the spell. Any Miscasts are applied to the unfortunate Skink Priest.
traits.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulties use core Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Palanquin
traits.text: On those occasions when Slann travel abroad, or accompany forces of Lizardmen, they sit atop stone palanquins that float above the earth thanks to ancient devices of forgotten design. These palanquins afford the following Creature Traits to the Slann: Fly 16, Ward 8+. In addition, the palanquin means that the Slann benefits from hard cover from missile fire originating from behind or to either side of the Slann, and soft cover from missile fire originating from in front of the Slann.

traits.name: Chariots of the Asur
traits.text: Only Swiftfeather Rocs willingly pull a Skycutter chariot, and an Elf’s reflexes are required to fly one safely and effectively.

traits.name: Blood Hungry Spore Cloud
traits.text: When disturbed by the movement of Human-sized or larger warm-blooded creatures occurring within one yard, the Bloated Pink Polypore emits a cloud of pale spores which cover an area with a 5-yard radius, 3 yards in height. The cloud persists for 2d10 Rounds. Any warm-blooded creature caught in this cloud must make a Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance Test or suffer 1 Bleeding Condition.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Impale Attack
traits.text: Attacks from the Impaling Spikethorn always target the legs of its opponent, without suffering the usual -20 penalty for called shots. They ignore leather armour and possess the Impale Weapon Quality.

traits.name: Entangled Attack
traits.text: Grasping Creeper Vine only attacks warm-blooded creatures. It may not use its Weapon attack against targets until it has inflicted an Entangled Condition upon them. Once the vine subjects its prey to an Entangled Condition, it strikes them once per turn with its Weapon attack until they break free or die.

traits.name: Magical Snack
traits.text: Itxi Grubs are edible (though they are an aquired taste). A spellcaster who consumes an Itxi Grub benefits from +1 SL to all Casting and Channelling Tests for the following 3d10 Rounds. This effect is not cumulative.

traits.name: Posterior Flame
traits.text: The Fireleech will resort to producing flames if it is subjected to stress such as being roughly handled, or suddenly disturbed by a warm-blooded creature. The Fireleech will produce a gout of flame that persists for 1d10 Rounds. During this time, any character or flammable item that is in contact with the Fireleech receives an Ablaze Condition.

traits.name: Use as Ammunition
traits.text: Cold-blooded creatures may handle Fireleeches by passing a Very Easy (+6 SL) Animal Care Test, and warm-blooded creatures by passing a Hard (−2 SL) Animal Care Test. Up to six Fireleeches can be stored in a damp leather pouch where, provided they are not jostled too badly, they will remain docile for 24 hours. A Character could throw a Fireleech or use it as ammunition for a sling. A second Animal Care Test must be passed to prepare the Fireleech. If this Test is failed, the Character trying to use the Fireleech as ammunition receives an Ablaze Condition. If the Test is successful, the Fireleech may be thrown or shot.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Brain Rot
traits.text: If a Brainfluke should ever inflict a Critical Hit upon the head of a warm-blooded opponent, then in addition to any Damage it inflicts, the Brainfluke burrows into the victim’s cranium and they contract the Brain Rot disease (see page 186).

traits.name: Excruciating Sting
traits.text: A Bloodwasp sting is notoriously painful. As long as the victim of a Bloodwasp sting suffers from any associated Poisoned Condition, they must struggle to ignore the terrible agony of the sting. They must pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test at the beginning of their Turn. If the Test is failed, they receive a Stunned Condition.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Odour Attack
traits.text: When harassed, these repulsive creatures are known to emit a noxious odour that spreads around the Toad to a distance of 1d10 yards. Any cold- blooded creature caught within the area must make a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test. Those who fail suffer from the Nausea Disease Symptom (WFRP, page 189) for 1d10 hours. Warm-blooded creatures notice a bad smell, but do not suffer from the symptom.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Scalemane Reptilion Venomous Bite
traits.text: The poisonous bite of a Scalemane Reptilion is particularly potent. Opponents affected by its Venom Trait take two Poisoned Conditions rather than the usual one.

traits.name: Blue-Ringed Asp Venomous Bite
traits.text: Opponents affected by its Venom Trait take a Bleeding Condition as well as a Poisoned Condition. The Bleeding Condition lasts until the Poisoned Condition is resolved.

traits.name: Boring Attack
traits.text: Attacks from Borer Snakes count as having the Damaging and Impale Qualities.

traits.name: Shooting Spine Attack
traits.text: Whether on the hunt or being prodded by Skinks during combat, Razordons can shoot their spines either singularly or en masse. It takes a day for the spines to regenerate.

traits.name: Unstoppable Charge
traits.text: A Stegadon gains +3 Momentum when they charge.
traits.adaptation: Old Advantage becomes Momentum; named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Ramming Attack
traits.text: Pliodons are known to sink river boats (perceived as a sort of rival predator) by ramming them repeatedly until the vessels take on water. Healthy Pliodons start with a Collision Rating of 14 when determining the results of this attack mode.

traits.name: Blood Frenzy
traits.text: Once a Carnosaur causes a Wound in combat, it immediately becomes Frenzied until all foes in range of its senses are slain.

traits.name: Toxic Bile
traits.text: Troglodons can project an acidic toxic bile up to 15 yards. The victim’s bile-caused wounds make a loud, sizzling sound as it burns, inflicting an Ablaze Condition on any Charcter hit by the bile).

traits.name: Fearsome Roar
traits.text: The Dread Saurian’s roar requires other Enormous- or Monstrous-Sized predators to pass a Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test. If failed, the affected creatures suffer from Fear and must depart the area immediately. Prey or other smaller creatures must pass a Hard (−2 SL) Cool Test to avoid fleeing in Fear.
traits.adaptation: Named Test Difficulties use Fifth Edition SL modifiers.

traits.name: Dooming
traits.text: The Dooming trait works as if the creature had the Blessed (Morr) Trait and access to the Dooming Miracle. However, Despairs are not beholden to any Human god, and while their abilities mirror those of priests of Morr, they are an innate talent of the Spites. The Spite uses its Willpower for Dooming, not the Invoke Talent.

mutations.name: Extra Mouth
mutations.text: Roll on the Hit Locations table to see where

mutations.name: Patchy Feathers
mutations.text: Roll on the Hit Locations table twice to see where

mutations.name: Spiny Protrusions
mutations.text: Roll on the Hit Locations table to see where

mutations.name: Uneven Horns
mutations.text: +1 Armour Point to Head; gain Horns

mutations.name: Whiskered Snout
mutations.text: Gain Acute Sense (Smell); +2 SL to Track Tests

mutations.name: Chaotic Dreams
mutations.text: Fatigued for the first two hours of each day

mutations.name: Hateful Impulses
mutations.text: Animosity towards all not of your Species

mutations.name: Shaky Morale
mutations.text: Gain Broken if you fail a Fear Test

mutations.name: Unending Malice
mutations.text: +1 SL on Tests to hurt; -1 SL to other Tests

training.name: Shock Cavalry
training.adaptation: The printed Challenging (+0) Dodge Test uses Fifth Edition Challenging (+0 SL), following core Appendix I p. 364.
training.text: Requires Trained (War). When Charging, a rider may move through smaller creatures to reach their target. Each trampled creature must make a Challenging (+0 SL) Dodge Test or suffer 4 + the mount’s Strength Bonus Damage. Each creature damaged reduces remaining Movement by 2 yards. Creatures the mount’s size or larger stop its progress. At the end of the Charge, enemies within melee range count as Engaged and the Charge is resolved as though one were its target. A smaller creature that has not acted this Round may forgo dodging to make one held-weapon attack against mount or rider. Unless that attack kills or disables the mount, the Charge continues.
